gloss: Physical movement of a person or entity from one place to another, on foot, by vehicle, or in pursuit of a target.
An emotional or attitudinal stance held toward, or emotional effect produced in, a person.
Producing a spoken or written statement that reports, discloses, or describes something.
Coming to have, or continuing to retain, possession of something.
A speech act aimed at directing or constraining someone else's future action.
Joining separate substances or objects into a single combined whole.
An entity spontaneously giving off light, sound, smell, or a substance.
Coming into being, being present, or happening, including atmospheric events.
Officially assigning or occupying a name, title, or role.
Forming, expressing, or assigning an evaluative opinion or value, including monetary worth.
Adopting a bodily posture or making a non-translational body movement or gesture.
Keeping away from, breaking free of, or deliberately not engaging in something.
Taking something away from a place, surface, or whole so that it is no longer there.
A reciprocal social relationship or joint activity between two or more parties.
Marking the beginning, continuation, duration, or ending of an event or state.
Putting on, wearing, or being in a state of dress.
The physical shape, posture, or spatial arrangement an entity holds or takes on.
An involuntary internal bodily sensation, function, or state change.
Tending to hair, teeth, or personal appearance.
Causing physical damage, injury, or death to an entity.
Causing another party to receive or have something, now or in the future.
Bringing something new into existence through effort, process, or performance.
Making physical contact with, or striking, something.
Causing a surface or container to become covered or full with a substance.
An entity's transition from one physical, biological, or circumstantial state to another.
Dividing or reshaping something with a blade or cutting action.
Concealing the truth or presenting a false appearance to others.
Taking in food, especially with attention to the manner or degree of consumption.
The style, medium, or nonverbal form through which communication is carried out.
Compelling, restricting, or controlling someone's action or scope.
Acting to protect or benefit another person.
Expressing a relation of similarity, difference, or relative magnitude between entities.
Directing attention or effort toward finding or coming to know something.
Forcefully propelling or directing an object, substance, or group into motion.
Placing or causing an entity to come to rest at a location.
Wanting or yearning for something.
Visually perceiving or looking at something.
Producing a written or documented record of something.
